nodes.label: cad2bim CAD-to-BIM Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Reads a structural CAD plan (DXF or Revit link), classifies layers, recovers/sizes/names every structural member from labels or schedules, and places them in Revit. Internal units are feet (mm/304.8); orchestrated by the CAD to BIM pushbutton script.py.

nodes.label: recover_core_walls_from_labels (Label-Guided Core Wall Carve)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over pure-geometry decomposition fixes because corners of fused wall blobs are genuinely ambiguous without labels: pure-geometry cell assignment reduced error 600->150mm but could not reach true positions; anchoring to blob outer edge did not generalize. The label-guided greedy-by-longest carve on a cell grid reconstructs Test19's true cover exactly and runs as a NEW pass BEFORE correct_columns_with_text so text-correction merely names already-correct walls.

nodes.label: Greedy Decomposition Corner-Stealing Bug
nodes.rationale: recover_rectilinear_columns assembles loose lines into a closed ring and decompose_to_rectangles greedily cuts it; the greedy cut steals shared corners so each wall is right-thickness but clipped/extended and offset. Root cause of Test19 lift-core mis-placement, C16 vanishing, and the markless stub vanishing.

nodes.label: correct_columns_with_text (Column Text Correction)
nodes.rationale: Resizes/names detected column geometry from nearby labels with grid snapping; its _is_split_pair/_merge_to_label path swallowed abutting neighbours (C16), which motivated running the label-guided carve before it. Uses an owner map so each label owns its nearest geometry.

nodes.label: build_beam_segments (Beam Detection)
nodes.rationale: Beam sources: closed thin outlines -> centerline; parallel line pairs one width apart -> midline; edge pairs against floor (slab-edge) lines; concentric arc-edge pairs -> curved beams. Beam detection is a Revit-link-polyline phenomenon: the DXF draws beams as loose lines, so offline debugging requires beams.raw_geometry replay. Too-wide outlines explode into the pair pool; a label can never rescue an out-of-range width.

nodes.label: _edge_pair_beams (Floor-Clipped Perimeter Beam Recovery)
nodes.rationale: Revit clips a perimeter beam's inner edge against the A-FLOR floor outline, so only ONE beam edge survives on S-BEAM and the floor edge is the partner edge. Pairs leftover beam lines with slab-edge lines and keeps a candidate only where an unplaced beam label of matching width sits across it; spatial dedup prevents floor re-traces from doubling beams. Candidate-label matching is ownership-based (nearest label) after the B4/B5 first-come swap bug.

nodes.label: Curved Beam Detection and Placement
nodes.rationale: A curved beam is two concentric arc EDGES, each a chain of short arc fragments, one beam width apart. _group_arc_edges clusters fragments (radius tolerance kept tight so inner/outer never merge); _curved_beams_from_edges pairs concentric edges whose radius gap is in the beam width band; _arc_span finds the swept angle as the complement of the largest circular gap; place_curved_beams places along Arc.Create.

nodes.label: Label-Owns-Segment Mark Matching
nodes.rationale: Label-claims-first (first-come) matching caused mark swaps (B4/B5) and mark theft (B23 beating B20). Marks are assigned by label-OWNS-segment on centreline distance, orientation-gated +-20 degrees because labels run ALONG their beam (MTEXT rotation is the text_direction vector, not dxf.rotation), with midpoint fallback for unclaimed segments.

nodes.label: snap_beam_ends_to_columns (Axial End Snap)
nodes.rationale: Beam ends snap ALONG the beam axis to the NEAREST round/rotated column's station -- never onto the centre point (off-axis columns would drag the beam sideways) and never first-match (two columns in reach collapsed B648 to zero length). Builder must recompute length from live endpoints post-snap or collapsed slivers throw 'Curve length too small'.

nodes.label: split_beams_at_columns (Beam-over-Column Discriminator)
nodes.rationale: Beam-column overlap has three shapes found by polygon-intersection census: strict interior crossing -> split at faces; segment buried face-to-face inside one column (column outline mis-read as beam) -> dropped; end drawn to the far face -> trimmed only when the end is >100mm PAST the column centre, because beams legitimately end AT centres. Regression-free guards: >=10mm midpoint penetration, <100mm leftovers dropped, untouched dicts reused so the pre-split slab snapshot stays valid, mark stays on the longest piece.

nodes.label: recover_outline_columns (Closed-Outline Column Authority)
nodes.rationale: Size limits protect against junk, but a CLOSED 4-corner column-layer outline with a plan mark beside it is a real column regardless of size (blade/wall columns 250x3250). Placed at drawn size/position/angle with no grid/size snapping; closedness IS the safety gate -- fragmented outlines stay unplaced. Downstream passes must also use drawn closed outlines as footprints, not just placed sections, or beam split goes blind exactly where blades are.

nodes.label: slab_outlines.py Slab Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Slab loops from A-FLOR rings (chained if loose), else the beam-perimeter graph (ends healed onto carriers, split at crossings, max-CCW face walk). Labels 'S1 150 THK' inside the loop size/name it; nested loops become floor openings. Chain tolerance trap: pieces shorter than the tolerance must be attached by globally-closest scoring over all four attach modes, and duplicate shared edges deduped by grid fingerprint first.

nodes.label: Placed-Geometry Slab Source (slab_loops_from_placed_members)
nodes.rationale: Slabs are created AFTER beams/columns, so outlines can be SYNTHESIZED from placed geometry (beam centreline +/- w/2 with end caps, column footprint rings) instead of re-parsing drawn linework -- alignment becomes exact by construction and the graph halves. Drawn edges still win where detection is incomplete; end caps only at FREE beam ends because junction caps deposit near-corner vertices that weld into jogs.

nodes.label: Exactness Pass (_snap_ring_to_carriers)
nodes.rationale: Weld-cluster centroids are approximations (up to snap/2 off the true junction); carriers are authority. The face walk decides TOPOLOGY only; positions are re-derived from authoritative input carriers: two-line crossing at corners, line x circle at wrap ends, radial mid-wrap. Carriers must be picked by ring-edge DIRECTION (topology), not proximity -- nearest-two grabbed a diamond column's 45-degree edges and welded boundaries onto the apex. Tessellated arc chords are never carriers.

nodes.label: Proximity-Clustering Node Identity
nodes.rationale: round(x/snap) grid-cell keys have a blind spot: points 44mm apart straddling a cell boundary stay separate while 49mm-apart points in one cell merge -- a dangling beam-edge tip got pruned and the bay face flooded over the beam body. Node identity must be union-find clustering over 3x3 neighbour cells, with cluster spread capped (~1.5x snap) so chained close vertices cannot swallow real geometry; tessellation must never emit chords shorter than ~2x snap.

nodes.label: Grid-Bucketed Pairwise Geometry Passes
nodes.rationale: All-pairs O(n^2) geometry passes do not survive real plans: _heal_endpoints/_split_at_crossings took 45.6s on ~4k edges; grid-bucket candidate pairs (3m cells, bbox prefilter) cut it to 2.1s. Any future pass touching pairwise segment geometry starts bucketed.

nodes.label: pythonnet IList Conversion Gotcha
nodes.rationale: Revit API IList<T> parameters do NOT accept Python lists under pythonnet: Floor.Create requires loops packed into System.Collections.Generic.List[CurveLoop]. This broke slab placement everywhere until v0.36.0.

nodes.label: Vendored Windows Wheels Fail on Linux
nodes.rationale: The numpy/ezdxf vendored under lib/py3 are Windows wheels: numpy calls os.add_dll_directory (Windows-only) and ezdxf then fails importing Vec3. Fix: pip install ezdxf to /tmp/pylibs first on sys.path, and pre-register anongee_toolkit as a bare namespace package so its Revit/.NET __init__ never runs -- the cad2bim subpackage itself is Revit-free.

nodes.label: replay_beams.py Offline Replay Harness
nodes.rationale: Because the DXF harness places ZERO beams (Revit's link reader merges loose lines into polylines), the JSON export dumps beams.raw_geometry and tests/replay_beams.py rebuilds CurveRecords and re-runs the real build_beam_segments offline -- every beam bug was pinned this way, with no guess-and-check Revit cycles.

nodes.label: Staircase Placement Pipeline (stair_layout.py + builders/stairs.py)

Enables running the real cad2bim pipeline and regression diffs (stash baseline vs new over all 15 DXF fixtures) on Linux without Revit.

nodes.label: 0.29.0 Stale-Build Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: All three 0.29.0 features absent together means none of the version is active = stale code, not a partial bug; script.py is re-read per click yet the deferred console was absent, so the RUNNING script.py is not the committed one -- pyRevit extensions often live in %APPDATA%/pyRevit, not the pulled git clone. The main window's version_text (set from cad2bim.__version__) is the decisive stale-vs-fresh check.

nodes.label: cad2bim Column & Beam Task Plan
nodes.rationale: Main goal: read a structural CAD plan, recover/size/name every structural member from its label or schedule, and place it in Revit. Columns complete (PR #4 merged via merge commit so the working branch stays cleanly ahead); beams, slabs, and staircases follow in phased rounds each closed by an offline regression diff and a Revit confirmation run.

nodes.label: Label-Guided Re-Tiling Decision
nodes.rationale: The core architectural decision: when abutting members share one drawn outline, greedy decomposition mis-cuts shared corners and the ambiguity cannot be resolved by geometry alone, so each fused blob is re-tiled FROM ITS LABELS before text-correction runs -- chosen over rewriting decompose (no labels there) or rewriting text-correction (too entangled). Carved walls are deliberately NOT grid-snapped: they sit at true drawn positions.

nodes.label: Zero-Regression Safety Gates
nodes.rationale: Gates that keep the carve zero-regression: only composite/recovered_strip blobs, component >= 2 pieces, blob must hold >= 1 MARKED label (a working markless-only core is never touched), and the carve must achieve a CLEAN FULL TILING or the blob is left exactly as decomposed (fallback = current behavior). Once firing it uses all sized labels so a sized markless stub packed into a marked blob places unnamed.
